methodology: Read Qur'an 11:81-85 in Arabic and Sahih International rendering; compared Genesis 19:12-29 in accessible Hebrew/English presentations. Hebrew critical edition, Greek/Syriac witnesses, and legal passages are not collated. Candidate associations explicitly hidden; no claim of borrowing.

ayahs.evidence_summary: Both describe angelic warning, departure, prohibition on looking back and Lot's wife. Genesis says she looked back and became a pillar of salt; Qur'an 11:81 says she shares the city's fate and specifies the morning. Genesis 19:15-16 describes a dawn departure; Qur'an instructs departure during the night.
Both narrate catastrophic divine destruction of the cities. Genesis specifies sulfur and fire; Qur'an describes overturning and stones of baked clay (sijjil). The mechanisms are not identical.
The marked stones and warning to wrongdoers are not individually matched to an earlier precise passage in this pass; Genesis 19:24-25 is only episode context.

Shu'ayb addresses Madyan and forbids dishonest measures. Earlier Israelite law also addresses fair measures, but its exact edition and original passage have not been independently checked this session; no identification of Shu'ayb with Jethro is inferred.

Full weight and measure and prohibition on depriving others resemble a broader ancient Near Eastern commercial-justice motif. Primary text and specific legal wording require comparison before any public association.

dossiers.title: Lot's escape and the destruction of the cities

source_table.edition: Hebrew Masoretic tradition; English translation version to be fixed
source_table.transmission: Genesis is an ancient composite text; surviving Masoretic manuscripts postdate its composition; Greek and Qumran witnesses require collation

dossiers.comparison: Angel-led rescue and city destruction are shared narrative episodes. The Qur'an specifies stones of sijjil and Lot's wife sharing the punishment; Genesis narrates sulfur and fire and the wife's transformation into salt. Avoid equating these details.

dossiers.title: Shu'ayb and commercial justice in Madyan
dossiers.comparison: Qur'anic prophetic warning concerning commercial fraud; compare legal prohibitions on false measures in the Hebrew Bible only after primary passage checking. The figure Shu'ayb must not automatically be identified with the Biblical Jethro.
